
"Your tea."

Evelyn set the cup her husband had asked for on the nightstand. Then she climbed into bed, pulled the blanket over herself, and turned onto her side with her back to Gavin, trying to sleep.

"Evie… are you asleep?" Gavin asked a little while later.

"Not yet," she said, without moving.

"I'm sorry."

That one word had stopped meaning anything to her. She wasn't angry the way she had been in the years before. She didn't cry anymore. She only lay still.

"I shouldn't have forgotten our anniversary. I really am a man you can't count on."

Gavin laughed, dry and hollow. Evelyn said nothing. Her soul had gone empty a long time ago. She couldn't even say when her feelings for him had quietly worn away to nothing.

"Tonight… did you make an anniversary dinner again? If you did, let's go down and eat. Even if it's cold by now, I'm sure it still tastes good."

He got out of bed, suddenly eager to head downstairs.

"I didn't cook anything."

Her voice froze his hand on the door. He turned back toward the bed.

His wife didn't stir. She hadn't shifted an inch from where she lay.

"Evelyn… what's wrong? Are you sick?"

Gavin came back and pressed the back of his hand to her forehead.

"Your temperature's normal. Is it your cramps again?"

His hand slid to her stomach, stroking the flat of it with what looked like tenderness.

"I'm fine," Evelyn said. She took his palm and lifted it off her.

"Evelyn…"

"I'm tired. May I rest now?"

"Of course. Good night."

Gavin kissed her forehead. He brushed her cheek and whispered, low, "I love you."

Except… Evelyn knew every word of it was a lie.

* * *

"Good morning, Evelyn!"

Vanessa's bright voice carried in from outside. As always, her sister had come to have breakfast at her house.

"So what are we eating this morning?" Vanessa asked, dragging out a chair and settling into it like she owned the place.

Evelyn took a loaf of plain bread from the refrigerator. She set it on the table, right in front of Vanessa.

"That's it?" Vanessa asked, one eyebrow arching high.

"That's all there is. If you want it, eat it. If not, go home," Evelyn said.

"You can't just throw your own sister out like that, sweetheart."

Gavin arrived to play peacemaker between them. But in Evelyn's eyes, he had only ever come to defend one person.

"Morning, Gavin," Vanessa said.

"Morning, Nessa," he answered, with a smile that meant far too much.

He joined them at the table, taking the chair directly beside Vanessa. Evelyn chose the seat across from them both.

"Sweetheart, you didn't make breakfast?" Gavin asked his wife, gently.

"No," Evelyn said shortly. She took a slice of bread, spread it with blueberry jam, and began eating it in small bites, though she wasn't especially hungry.

"Why not? You know Vanessa has to eat something before work."

Evelyn's brow creased. "Since when did her breakfast become my responsibility?"

Gavin stiffened. Vanessa let out an irritated little growl.

"Evie, are you upset that I keep having breakfast here? Do you think I'm a burden?"

"Good. I'm glad you're finally aware of it."

"Evelyn!" Gavin barked at his wife. The only thing he cared about was the way Vanessa's face shifted from a smile into something wounded.

"Vanessa is your sister. Is that any way to speak to her?"

Evelyn said nothing. She had no interest in arguing. However loud she got, Gavin would never once hear her side of it.

"Now apologize to Vanessa," Gavin ordered.

"Gavin…" Vanessa stroked his arm, slow and deliberate, staging the whole tender little scene for Evelyn's benefit.

"…Evelyn hasn't done anything wrong. I have. I shouldn't keep imposing on the two of you. Starting tomorrow, I'll eat at my own house. I won't come here for breakfast anymore."

"Are you satisfied now, Evelyn?"

Gavin's voice still had anger in it. "It was such a small thing. What's the harm in one extra plate for your own sister?"

"Maybe Evelyn's just tired," Vanessa put in. "You have to understand. Housework may not wear you out the way office work does, but she's still working hard keeping this place running. Isn't that right, Evelyn?"

Vanessa tilted her head. The look in her eyes was pure mockery, pure challenge. But Evelyn wasn't so easily baited.

"Stop defending her all the time, Nessa. She's stubborn like this because you spoil her too much."

Gavin snorted. He took a slice of bread, spread it with chocolate, and handed it to Vanessa.

"Eat this for now — that's all right, isn't it?"

"Thank you, Gavin."

Vanessa smiled wide.

"What would you like for breakfast tomorrow?"

"I'd love a sandwich with smoked beef."

"Evelyn — you heard that, didn't you?"

Once again Evelyn didn't answer. When her bread was gone, she rose and left the table.

She walked into a room set beside the storeroom. It was soundproof, and she locked it tight from the inside.

Evelyn switched on the two televisions mounted on the wall. She sat down, picked up a pair of headphones, and listened to the audio of the video already playing.

A video of her husband and her sister, still sitting at the breakfast table, so close and so intimate.

CCTV.

*"Nessa, are you happy, married to Damian?"*

On the screen, Gavin held both of Vanessa's hands. His gaze was soft, full of love.

*"And if I said I wasn't — what would you do about it?"*

Vanessa's voice came back mournful.

*"Why aren't you happy?"*

Gavin sounded almost desperate.

*"Didn't you promise me you'd be happy once you married him? I gave up everything for the sake of your happiness. I was willing to marry Evelyn just to make sure she'd never get in the way of you and Damian."*

*"Gavin, being married to Damian isn't the fairy tale I imagined. At first everything felt perfect. But little by little, he started showing his true colors. He's too controlling. He boxes me in. He even forces me to work to help support the household — when all I ever wanted was to be a stay-at-home wife, like Evelyn. I want to welcome my husband home every evening. I want to cook for him. I want every hour of my day to belong to my family."*

Vanessa smiled. Her cunning was slowly clicking back into gear.

In the beginning, Gavin had loved her deeply. But because Vanessa had chosen Damian instead, she'd turned Gavin's feelings away.

Now, though, Vanessa was bored with Damian. She didn't want a man who told her to go out and work.

She wanted a man like Gavin. A man who'd ask nothing of her but to sit pretty at home, never once feeling the exhaustion of earning her own way.

*"Gavin…"* On the screen, Vanessa touched his face. *"…if I'd married you back then, would my life be as happy as Evelyn's?"*

And Evelyn, watching all of it, only stared, expressionless. Whatever she'd once felt for Gavin was, perhaps, truly finished now.
